newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina plans to cut 15,000 state jobs - report.
newsitem.headline: Argentina plans to cut 15,000 state jobs - report.

text.p: Argentina's government has drawn up a decree to lay off or transfer at least 15,000 state employees in a major administrative reorganization to cut costs, the Clarin daily reported Tuesday.
Up to 27,000 public servants could lose their jobs in coming months, according to the document, which Clarin said it consulted at the International Monetary Fund meeting in Washington.
Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez told Clarin in Washington -- "The project is ready and when we return by the weekend it will be signed."

Dismissed public servants will receive payments from a special government retraining fund for up to six months if they have been employed for 15 years or less, and for up to a year if they have worked for 30 years.

The fund was set up under the government's Second Reform of the State, passed early this year, which also granted special powers to the executive to decree dismissals and the abolition of government departments.
